This Quarto notebook is the canonical executable source for
`scripts/inspect_16s_quality_profiles.qmd`. It profiles the primer-removed
reads and turns truncation from a habit into a recorded decision: the length
budget must leave enough overlap to merge the amplicon, and the quality tail
must not be carried into the error model.

```sh
bash scripts/run_qmd.sh scripts/inspect_16s_quality_profiles.qmd [trimmed_dir] [output_dir]
```

Automatic execution during rendering is disabled because this workflow writes
project outputs.

```{r}
#| label: inspect-16s-quality-profiles
#| echo: true
abort <- function(...) stop(sprintf(...), call. = FALSE)

args <- commandArgs(trailingOnly = TRUE)
trimmed_dir <- if (length(args) >= 1L) args[[1L]] else Sys.getenv("PHAGE_UV_16S_TRIMMED_DIR")
output_dir <- if (length(args) >= 2L) args[[2L]] else Sys.getenv("PHAGE_UV_16S_QUALITY_DIR")
if (!nzchar(trimmed_dir) || !nzchar(output_dir)) {
  abort("Provide trimmed_dir and output_dir, or source config/16s_analysis_paths.sh first.")
}
for (pkg in c("dada2", "ShortRead", "ggplot2")) {
  if (!requireNamespace(pkg, quietly = TRUE)) abort("Package %s is required.", pkg)
}
dir.create(output_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)

forward <- sort(list.files(trimmed_dir, pattern = "_R1\\.trimmed\\.fastq\\.gz$", full.names = TRUE))
reverse <- sort(list.files(trimmed_dir, pattern = "_R2\\.trimmed\\.fastq\\.gz$", full.names = TRUE))
if (!length(forward) || length(forward) != length(reverse)) {
  abort("Expected matched R1/R2 trimmed FASTQs in %s; found %d and %d.",
        trimmed_dir, length(forward), length(reverse))
}

# Aggregated quality profiles across all samples, then per-sample panels.
pdf(file.path(output_dir, "16s_quality_profiles.pdf"), width = 9, height = 6)
print(dada2::plotQualityProfile(forward, aggregate = TRUE) +
        ggplot2::ggtitle("Forward reads, aggregated"))
print(dada2::plotQualityProfile(reverse, aggregate = TRUE) +
        ggplot2::ggtitle("Reverse reads, aggregated"))
print(dada2::plotQualityProfile(forward))
print(dada2::plotQualityProfile(reverse))
invisible(dev.off())

# Per-cycle quality summary computed directly from the FASTQs, so the chosen
# truncation points are reproducible from a table rather than read off a plot.
cycle_summary <- function(files, direction, sample_n = 50000L) {
  quality_matrix <- NULL
  for (file in files) {
    sampler <- ShortRead::FastqSampler(file, n = sample_n)
    reads <- ShortRead::yield(sampler)
    close(sampler)
    scores <- methods::as(Biostrings::quality(reads), "matrix")
    if (is.null(quality_matrix)) {
      quality_matrix <- scores
    } else {
      width <- max(ncol(quality_matrix), ncol(scores))
      pad <- function(m, w) {
        if (ncol(m) == w) return(m)
        cbind(m, matrix(NA_integer_, nrow = nrow(m), ncol = w - ncol(m)))
      }
      quality_matrix <- rbind(pad(quality_matrix, width), pad(scores, width))
    }
  }
  data.frame(
    read_direction = direction,
    cycle = seq_len(ncol(quality_matrix)),
    reads_scored = apply(quality_matrix, 2, function(x) sum(!is.na(x))),
    median_quality = apply(quality_matrix, 2, stats::median, na.rm = TRUE),
    q25_quality = apply(quality_matrix, 2, stats::quantile, probs = 0.25, na.rm = TRUE),
    mean_quality = round(colMeans(quality_matrix, na.rm = TRUE), 3),
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )
}

cycles <- rbind(cycle_summary(forward, "R1"), cycle_summary(reverse, "R2"))
write.table(cycles, file.path(output_dir, "16s_per_cycle_quality.tsv"),
            sep = "\t", quote = FALSE, row.names = FALSE)

# Last cycle at which the median quality still meets a threshold. This is a
# candidate truncation point, not an automatic decision.
last_cycle_at <- function(direction, threshold) {
  sub <- cycles[cycles$read_direction == direction & cycles$median_quality >= threshold, ]
  if (!nrow(sub)) return(NA_integer_)
  max(sub$cycle)
}
thresholds <- c(30, 28, 25, 20)
candidates <- data.frame(
  median_quality_threshold = thresholds,
  trunc_len_r1 = vapply(thresholds, function(q) last_cycle_at("R1", q), integer(1)),
  trunc_len_r2 = vapply(thresholds, function(q) last_cycle_at("R2", q), integer(1)),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

# Overlap budget. The primer-free insert is the amplicon minus both primers.
# The original methods report an approximately 550 bp amplicon, while the
# 515F/907R product is usually near 410 bp. Both hypotheses are carried here
# because the merge rate in step 4 is what settles the question empirically.
primer_bases <- nchar(Sys.getenv("PHAGE_UV_16S_PRIMER_FWD", "GTGYCAGCMGCCGCGGTAA")) +
  nchar(Sys.getenv("PHAGE_UV_16S_PRIMER_REV", "CCCCGYCAATTCMTTTRAGT"))
min_overlap <- as.integer(Sys.getenv("PHAGE_UV_16S_MIN_OVERLAP", "20"))
amplicon_hypotheses <- c(literature_515f_907r = 410L, original_methods_statement = 550L)

planning <- do.call(rbind, lapply(names(amplicon_hypotheses), function(hypothesis) {
  insert <- amplicon_hypotheses[[hypothesis]] - primer_bases
  out <- candidates
  out$amplicon_hypothesis <- hypothesis
  out$assumed_amplicon_bp <- amplicon_hypotheses[[hypothesis]]
  out$assumed_insert_bp <- insert
  out$expected_overlap_bp <- out$trunc_len_r1 + out$trunc_len_r2 - insert
  out$meets_min_overlap <- !is.na(out$expected_overlap_bp) & out$expected_overlap_bp >= min_overlap
  out
}))
planning <- planning[, c("amplicon_hypothesis", "assumed_amplicon_bp", "assumed_insert_bp",
                         "median_quality_threshold", "trunc_len_r1", "trunc_len_r2",
                         "expected_overlap_bp", "meets_min_overlap")]
write.table(planning, file.path(output_dir, "16s_truncation_planning.tsv"),
            sep = "\t", quote = FALSE, row.names = FALSE)

print(planning)
cat(sprintf("\nWrote quality profiles, per-cycle table, and truncation planning to %s\n", output_dir))
cat("Set PHAGE_UV_16S_TRUNC_LEN_R1 and PHAGE_UV_16S_TRUNC_LEN_R2 from this table before step 4.\n")
cat("Any pair whose expected overlap fails under BOTH hypotheses must not be used.\n")
```
